clue.text: Date of battle

definitions.meaning: an appointment or arranged meeting, especially a romantic one
a fight between armed forces, a military action

explanation.definitionFit: A date is a social commitment one has made, and a clash of armies is also called by the same military term.

clue.text: Catch a glimpse of eastern agent

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A traveller briefly spots an operative from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to sight or notice something, often at a distance.

clue.text: Try to support little bird

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try
a sling supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: Advice to prop up a small injured bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A gosling is a young goose, so a small bird in the sense of a baby one.

clue.text: In this pass, directors are ignored

definitions.text: In this pass, directors are ignored

parts.words: In this pass, directors are ignored
parts.note: read literally, a company's directors sit on a board, and passing by that board means ignoring them; the idiom means to be abandoned or neglected

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes plans or principles that are dropped or neglected, passed by as unimportant.

clue.text: Test tree lights in this

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match, so test gives the word for a game
box is an evergreen tree or shrub used for hedging

explanation.surface: An instruction to check a tree's illuminations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' is the noun for matches: an old word for things used to light a fire, and the answer holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: Matches, once commonly called lights, are kept in a small cardboard container.

clue.text: Fool can end in the soup

definitions.meaning: strips of pasta often finish up in a bowl of broth

explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a dimwit and also names the strips of pasta found in chicken broth.

clue.text: Bird not in drag

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the word in out of the bird's name

parts.note: the puffin is a seabird with a colourful beak
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird that refuses to dress up in women's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' is not cross-dressing but a draw on a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag on a cigarette is a single inhalation, also called a pull.

clue.text: Leading firm on the defensive

parts.note: to be up is to be ahead, leading in a game
firm means taut or secure

explanation.surface: A team ahead in the match holds firm in defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tense and nervous is guarded and anxious, defensive in manner.

clue.text: Prophet with warning to impart to the king

parts.note: fore is the warning shouted by golfers
to impart news is to tell it
ER can stand for Edward Rex, the royal cipher of a King Edward

explanation.surface: A seer brings a warning to pass on to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the warning a golfer shouts; ER (Edward Rex) is a king's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet predicts what will happen, a seer of the future.

clue.text: Manual control to unlock, not shut, pub

indicators.note: unlocking frees the letters of the three words to fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions on opening a pub's door when it isn't closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to unlock' shuffles the letters of NOT SHUT PUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A device worked by pressing with a finger is operated by hand, a manually worked switch.

clue.text: Pooh, making a comeback, is brilliant

indicators.note: making a comeback suggests going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: pooh and rats are both exclamations of annoyance

explanation.surface: A bear returning to fame shines once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pooh' is the dismissive exclamation, not the bear; RATS read backwards gives the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Star used as an adjective means outstanding, top-class.

clue.text: Learned lady got buckles in tangle

indicators.note: a tangle is a muddle, so the letters are jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who has caught her shoe buckles in a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: The term, often dismissive, describes an intellectual or literary woman.

clue.text: Composer, we hear, is a heel

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and pianist

explanation.surface: A slur on a musician as a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' is not a cad but the verb used of a ship leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels tilts to one side, which sailors also call leaning.

clue.text: In the gloaming Henry takes wing

parts.note: Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as for Shakespeare's Prince Hal
flight, as in the power of flying on wings, or an air force unit

explanation.surface: Henry flies off at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: The gloaming is twilight, the dim light of dusk.

clue.text: Dissatisfied with Cheshire, perhaps remove

parts.note: Cheshire is an English cheese, so an example of the category
to doff a hat is to remove it

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with the county of Cheshire wants to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is an English county, but here it is the cheese made there.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for annoyed and fed up, disgruntled.

clue.text: French Protestant starts off homily using foreign tongue

indicators.note: the starts of the two words homily and using are taken
foreign suggests something strange, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sermon delivered in a foreign language.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was given to French Calvinists of the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: The cost of housing books in old money

indicators.note: in places the books inside the coin's name

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish and Portuguese coin
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Home costs paid in former currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like the container signal but belongs to the definition; 'in' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the payment for occupying a home or property.

clue.text: Board admit necessity to be much involved

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: board, as in food and lodging, is one's keep
a need is a necessity

explanation.surface: A company board concedes something is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deeply engaged in something, figuratively waist-high in it.

clue.text: Half of them dodge being put to work

indicators.note: the second half of the word them is taken

parts.note: a dodge is a trick or ploy

explanation.surface: Half of a group shirk their tasks when given work.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire or engage someone is to give them a job.

clue.text: Yak, new style

parts.note: yak is slang for chatter, and patter is glib talk

explanation.surface: A Himalayan ox in a fresh fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yak' looks like the Tibetan ox but is the verb meaning chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A design or model is a style or template.

clue.text: Flighty daughter leaves town

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire, England

explanation.surface: A capricious daughter moves out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: DUNSTABLE is a town in Bedfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flighty is fickle and erratic, not steady.

clue.text: The defence obtains a different order…

indicators.note: putting the letters in a different order means rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A defence team gets a new set of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a fortified projection of a rampart, a stronghold of defence.

clue.text: …calling for haste

definitions.meaning: to rush along at speed, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue's surface; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a lifelong profession and also, as a verb, to rush headlong.

clue.text: Demolish a pretext I concocted

indicators.note: concocted means made up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An excuse invented to justify knocking something down.
explanation.definitionFit: To extirpate is to root out or destroy completely.

clue.text: Pitch-and-toss players

definitions.meaning: to pitch and to toss are both to throw

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to throw, and also the company of actors in a play.

clue.text: Girl enlisted in the German navy

indicators.note: enlisted in means serving within, so the name is found inside the words German navy

explanation.surface: A young woman joining the German fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name used as an example.

clue.text: Frank makes love to Penelope

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, shaped like O
Pen is a short form of Penelope; that the letters also run across 'to Penelope' is a coincidence, with no indicator for a hidden word

explanation.surface: Frank woos a woman called Penelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means candid and honest, with nothing hidden.

clue.text: Engineers request a going-over

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a petition is a formal request

explanation.surface: Army engineers ask for a review.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over something again is doing it once more, a rerun.

clue.text: Penalty conceded by back provided two points

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for provided in reverse

parts.note: provided means if, as a condition
N and E are two points of the compass, north and east

explanation.surface: A football full-back gives away a penalty in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a defender but turns IF round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine is a monetary punishment, a penalty paid.

clue.text: Information has characteristic look, some might say

indicators.note: some might say signals a pronunciation of a phrase

parts.note: a proper gander is a typical good look, gander being slang for a glance

explanation.surface: A person's distinctive glance carries a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' is British slang for a look; 'proper' means typical, so 'proper gander' said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is information, often biased, spread to promote a cause.
